points.description: States that an SVM is a (linear) classifier that finds a decision boundary / separating hyperplane between classes by maximizing the margin (maximum-margin classifier).

levels.says: Mentions only a decision boundary/hyperplane separating classes, or only 'large margin', without linking maximum margin to the boundary choice.

points.description: States that the support vectors are the data points closest to the decision boundary (on the margin) and that they determine/define the margin and hyperplane. Equivalent wording accepted. Using the term 'support vectors' is required for full marks.

levels.says: Describes points nearest the boundary determining the margin but does not name them support vectors (or names them without saying what they are/do).

rubric.notes: Full marks: maximum-margin decision boundary/hyperplane (1) plus support vectors as the nearest points defining the margin (1). Half of a point if the idea is present but the key term or link is missing. Kernels and quadratic programming are optional extras and earn no additional marks.
